arguments.summary: Technical read as of the 2026-09-22 completed session: ANET has strong absolute momentum and 21-/63-session leadership, but not uniform near-term leadership—its 5-session return beat SPY yet trailed XLK slightly. Price is above rising short-, medium- and long-term averages and near the prior 21-session closing high, while elevated realized volatility and a 15.5060% maximum 63-session close-path drawdown show substantial path risk. Historical analogs in the current coarse trend regime had positive-return frequencies of 55.4517%, 63.8629% and 65.7321% over 5, 21 and 63 sessions, respectively; each was below its unconditional base rate. These are dependent, overlapping historical observations, not calibrated forecasts. The setup therefore supports conditional continuation, not a high-confidence probability claim.

claims.text: On 2026-09-22, ANET closed at $205.19 on the split-adjusted SIP series. Its price returns were +6.4043% over 5 sessions, +8.7676% over 21 and +26.5043% over 63. The close was 1.0495x SMA20, 1.0892x SMA50 and 1.3162x SMA200; RSI14 was 63.6177. This is absolute price strength, not by itself benchmark leadership or intrinsic value evidence.

Matched-return rows: PAIR ANET/SPY 5=+4.2931 21=+7.7672 63=+21.0789; PAIR ANET/XLK 5=-0.4151 21=+1.6976 63=+19.9459. Thus ANET led SPY at all three measured windows, but versus XLK it moved from a slight 5-session lag to 21- and 63-session outperformance. A recent rebound can therefore coexist with mixed very-short-window sector leadership and strong longer-window leadership.

The current historical-regime definition is close above SMA20, SMA20 above SMA50 and positive 21-session return. Conditional positive-return frequency was 55.4517% (178/321) over 5 sessions, with p10/median/p90 of -7.5762%/+0.4974%/+6.7425%, versus an unconditional 58.6207% (374/638) base rate. At 21 sessions it was 63.8629% (205/321), with -12.6204%/+2.8939%/+15.5652%, versus 68.3386% (436/638). At 63 sessions it was 65.7321% (211/321), with -20.6472%/+10.6427%/+36.7049%, versus 75.3918% (481/638). These overlapping forward windows come from one finite 2023-12-05 to 2026-06-23 history, are statistically dependent, and are empirical analog frequencies—not calibrated forecasts, causal estimates or guarantees.

ANET's 5-, 21- and 63-session annualized realized volatility was 22.4371%, 44.8032% and 55.0458%. The maximum 63-session close-path drawdown was -15.5060%, while the 2026-09-22 close was 2.5226% below the 252-session high. These are observed path-risk measures, not an earnings-risk coefficient or future volatility forecast.

Over the latest five sessions, SMA20 rose 1.7405%. The last close was only 0.1120% below the prior 21-session closing high. Last-session volume was 0.9803x the prior 20-session median, although recent five-session average volume was 1.3679x that median. This shows price pressing near a prior high with elevated recent average activity, but the single latest volume reading does not establish sustained breakout confirmation.

Continuation case: positive returns across all three windows, a rising SMA20, price above SMA20/SMA50/SMA200 and positive 21-/63-session excess returns versus both SPY and XLK indicate a constructive trend with established medium-horizon leadership. The competing explanation is that ANET is participating in a strong technology rebound rather than beginning a fresh stock-specific leg: it slightly lagged XLK over 5 sessions, remains just below the prior 21-session closing high, and its historical current-regime frequencies are below unconditional base rates at every requested horizon. The implication is to require continued relative leadership and level confirmation rather than extrapolate the rebound.

gaps.description: Stronger breakout conviction requires subsequent completed-session evidence: sustained closes through the prior 21-session closing high, repeated—not one-day—volume context, and recomputed matched-window excess returns. The supplied snapshot cannot establish persistence.

assumptions: All comparisons use completed sessions through 2026-09-22, SIP feed, split-adjusted prices and price-return basis.

The historical regime is intentionally coarse; a close below SMA20, SMA20 below SMA50, or non-positive 21-session return would move ANET outside the sampled current regime and invalidate direct use of these conditional analog statistics.
Forward-return observations overlap, so sample counts are not independent trials; no subjective probability or expected return is inferred.
The completed-close threshold is a frozen 2026-09-22 SMA20 level, not a future dynamically recomputed moving average and not an order instruction.
arguments.counter_thesis: The apparent leadership may be a volatile rebound embedded in broad technology strength rather than durable ANET leadership. Evidence for that interpretation would be failure to clear and hold the prior 21-session closing high, a completed close below the frozen $195.506 SMA20 level, and a reversal of matched 21-session excess returns to negative versus both SPY and XLK; if 63-session excess also turns negative, the longer-window leadership thesis would be invalidated.

review_conditions.description: If ANET records a completed split-adjusted close below the frozen 2026-09-22 SMA20 level of $195.506 before expiry, treat short-term trend support as broken and downgrade the continuation interpretation to neutral/cautious pending a fresh path-panel calculation.

Recompute matched 21- and 63-session price-return excess versus both SPY and XLK. If 21-session excess turns negative against both while 63-session excess stays positive, interpret it as near-term leadership fatigue but intact longer-window leadership; if both 21- and 63-session excess are negative against both benchmarks, invalidate the current leadership setup. Continued positive signs at both windows would confirm persistence.
